parsed.explanation: Adult alone faces Reduced Risk: no criminalisation of trans life, federal protection of gender identity, a 2024 damages ruling recognising trans women as women, and 2025 hate-crime penalties make post-discovery severity moderate-low. Exposure arises from marker/document mismatch, organised anti-trans campaigns, facilities/records disputes and uneven state coverage. Functioning courts mediate social hostility, but current border/marker rules and custody practice outside one state are unknown. Trans minors and guardians face lower safety because one state restricted new under-18 prescriptions, though existing patients are exempt and the directive was judicially challenged. Integrated rating weights adult safety but reflects the age-dependent care exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry refusal documented. 2003 brief records sex-marker friction on passports, licences and certificates; current border/marker rules unknown, leaving mismatch risk at ID checks.
entry_documents.protection: Home passport controls entry; no criminalisation; federal sex-discrimination law supports service and document complaints.
entry_documents.interaction: A document-presentation mismatch could surface at immigration, hotel check-in, banking or emergency services.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Custody placement documented only for one state; staff discretion and a surgery exception create gaps; other jurisdictions’ practice is not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2022 detention standards in one state direct admission to lived/experienced-gender facilities; no trans-specific crime.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention would expose a traveller to jurisdiction-dependent placement and frontline discretion.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Organised exclusionary campaigns and documented disputes over facilities and records; state/territory gender-identity coverage is uneven.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Federal sex-discrimination protection; 2024 court damages; national hate-crime law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local gaps may encourage denial, but federal remedy likely limits severity.

care_services.exposure: Adult HRT continuity undocumented; one state restricts new under-18 blocker/hormone prescriptions; surgery cost/waiting gaps.
care_services.protection: National health scheme covers many surgeries; child framework permits agreed treatment; no documented adult refusal.
care_services.interaction: Restrictions are age-dependent, mainly affecting minors and guardians.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Rights-rollback pressure and targeted activism frame trans people as contested; no hate-crime prosecution data.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime penalties up to seven years; damages awarded; apprehended-violence order against an activist.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State/local hostility can escalate encounters; courts have intervened.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor in the restricted state may be denied new blockers/hormones; care-seeking can out the child or guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: Existing patients exempt; court ruled directive unlawful; challenge filed; national framework permits treatment.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travel through that state is the main age-dependent exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2003 research and 2024 order show harassment/assault risk; current frequency and police response data unknown.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime law, anti-discrimination, pride-city culture; no documented state targeting of trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local campaigns could worsen street incidents where state protections are weaker.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Missing prosecution data, unresolved state reforms, unknown current marker rules and custody practice in other jurisdictions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Court damages, active legal challenge, detention standards and federal complaints indicate functioning remedies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Known relief lowers severity; gaps sustain uncertainty rather than safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Below 0.85-A: national protections and remedies exist, but visitor passport/marker acceptance, uniform facilities, and border protocols are not documented; organised campaigns raise visible risk.
Near 0.75-A: adult care and anti-discrimination are protective, yet youth-care restrictions and uneven state coverage keep it slightly below this anchor.

At/above 0.65-E: no routine invasive border medical questioning is documented and remedies work; subnational facility disputes and minor-care limits add exposure but do not reach detention-heavy risk.
Far above 0.55-B: no registration/checkpoint system is documented and national law/courts provide remedies, though marker friction remains unresolved.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a protective national layer with contested state pockets. Federal anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, recent civil damages, and at least one detention standard for lived-gender placement reduce the consequences of outing for adult travellers. State campaigns, uneven vilification coverage, historic document friction and missing prosecution data keep exposure above a clear low-risk setting. A minor traveller’s care pathway is the sharpest age-dependent interaction: one jurisdiction’s prescription restriction can force disclosure and delay treatment, but exemption and court challenge limit severity.
